title: Rational Canonical Form: Companion Matrix (Complete Proof)

problemStatement.formal: \text{For a monic polynomial } p \in R[X] \text{ of degree } n, \text{ let } C(p) \text{ be the companion matrix. Prove } p(C(p)) = 0,\ \minpoly(C(p)) = p,\ \text{and } \charpoly(C(p)) = p.
problemStatement.plain: The companion matrix C(p) is built from the coefficients of a monic polynomial p, with 1s on the subdiagonal and negated coefficients in the last column. The goal is to prove that this matrix fully encodes p: it is annihilated by p, and both its minimal and characteristic polynomials are exactly p.
whyMatters: Companion matrices are the fundamental blocks of rational canonical form.
Completing this proof supports the full rational canonical form theorem and the bridge between module structure and Jordan/RCF theory.

proven: `companionMatrix_last_col_entry`: last column entries are negative polynomial coefficients.
`companionMatrix_linear`: C(X - c) = [c] in the linear polynomial case.

knowledge.markdown:
# Knowledge Base: cayley-hamilton-reduction-oq-02-oq-01-incomplete-01

## Problem Understanding

The goal is to finish the companion matrix proof used by rational canonical form. For a monic polynomial p and its companion matrix C(p), the remaining statements are p(C(p)) = 0, minpoly(C(p)) = p, and charpoly(C(p)) = p.

## Existing Infrastructure

The notes list proven lemmas for the companion matrix subdiagonal entries, last-column entries, the linear-polynomial case, and the orbit chain for basis vectors under C(p). Mathlib also has Matrix.aeval_self_charpoly available.

## Open Work

Three sorry statements remain in proofs/Proofs/CayleyHamiltonReductionOQ02OQ01.lean. The intended path is to complete the orbit computation for p(C(p)) = 0, then use minpoly divisibility and degree/monicity facts to identify the minimal and characteristic polynomials.
